# `get_comet_position`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

List current comet positions, optionally filtered to one comet by exact name.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (both builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb3680, GetCometData @0x13a3b0 (callers get_comet_position, SortTarget @0x30e7a0 name match only, AutoSavePlan @0x30ea00 reads ra/dec @0x31060c) (64-bit build) |

Runs a supplied ephemeris script synchronously and parses its scratch output. The user location is loaded, or on failure fetched from the guider connection. Positions are computed on the device for that site at the current time (no refraction); ra and dec are apparent coordinates of date, not J2000, and size is the apparent diameter in arcseconds (INFERRED from the ephemeris library). The device only echoes size; the plan runner reads only ra and dec of a comet (READ). A success result is a non-empty array; if the final list is empty the call fails with 207. A regex failure partway through can still return the rows parsed so far as a success. Classified C because the location fallback can reconnect the guider and re-apply the LED state.

Side effects: Writes a scratch ephemeris output file and logs. If loading the stored location fails, falls back to a guider geographic query which can trigger a guider reconnect callback that sends a movement-scale/ratio update and re-applies the power LED. No timeout and no mode or park guard.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_comet_position"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string | no | - | Optional comet-name filter. Only a JSON string is used: exact, case-sensitive, full-length match. An empty string is a real filter (matches nothing useful), not the default. Absent params or any other type (object, array, null, number, boolean) means an unfiltered query; there is no positional-array conversion and no error for the wrong type. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 214 | The script command cannot be started | `fail to run command` |
| 258 | The scratch output file cannot be opened | `open file failed` |
| 207 | Malformed ephemeris data, or the final comet list is empty (zero error normalised to 207) | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Location-helper error leakage and script failures masked by a successful command start are unresolved.

## Example

Request, all:

```json
{"id":111,"method":"get_comet_position"}
```

Request, filtered:

```json
{"id":112,"method":"get_comet_position","params":"Example Comet"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_comet_position","result":[{"id":0,"name":"Example Comet","mag":9.5,"ra":5.25,"dec":12.5,"size":3.2}],"code":0,"id":111}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_comet_position","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":113}
```
